summary.text: Hiroshima is the capital of Hiroshima Prefecture in Japan, a city founded in 1589 as a castle town on the Ōta River delta.
On 6 August 1945 the United States Army Air Forces dropped the atomic bomb "Little Boy" on it, making it the first military target of a nuclear weapon in history.
Most of the city was destroyed, and by the end of the year between 90,000 and 166,000 people had died from the blast and its effects.

facts.label: A-Bomb Dome
facts.value: The only structure left standing, kept as a preserved ruin

items.prompt: Hiroshima is mentioned in history books for a grim "first". What was it?

options.label: It was the first city to use rail for troops
It was the first target of any air raid
It was the first military target of a nuclear weapon
It was the first city to surrender in 1945

items.explain: Hiroshima was the first military target of a nuclear weapon in history, on 6 August 1945.

items.prompt: In 1894 a rail line was built from Hiroshima's main station to its harbour. What was it for?

options.label: Carrying cotton from the new mills
Military transportation during the First Sino-Japanese War
Bringing visitors to the castle
Moving goods for the trade exhibition

items.explain: The line was built for military transportation during the First Sino-Japanese War.

items.prompt: What stimulated further industrialisation in Hiroshima in 1904?

options.label: The Russo-Japanese War and its need for military supplies
The founding of a new government school for English
The move of the Emperor's headquarters to the city
A rail link opened to the city's busy harbour

items.explain: The Russo-Japanese War of 1904 required development and production of military supplies.

items.prompt: A warlord who founded a castle town backs the losing side in a major battle. What happens to his lands?

options.label: He keeps them after paying a fine
They pass to his oldest son at once
The Emperor divides them among villages
The winner takes most of his fiefs, including Hiroshima

items.explain: Tokugawa Ieyasu deprived Mōri Terumoto of most of his fiefs, including Hiroshima, after Sekigahara.

items.prompt: A building opened in 1915 to host trade and show new products is now preserved as what?

options.label: The castle that Mōri Terumoto built
The A-Bomb Dome, part of the Hiroshima Peace Memorial
The temple of Mitaki-dera
A mill from the 1800s

items.explain: The 1915 hall, renamed several times, is now the A-Bomb Dome, a preserved ruin in the Peace Memorial.

items.prompt: What was the area like before the 1589 castle town was founded?

options.label: A small fishing village on Hiroshima Bay tied to a Zen temple
A large port town ruled by the Asano clan
A walled capital of a prefecture
A garrison town built for the army

items.explain: The area was originally a small fishing village along Hiroshima Bay, economically attached to the Zen Buddhist temple Mitaki-dera.
